translations.text: THE CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. I WILL GIVE THANKS TO YOU, LORD, BECAUSE YOU WERE ANGRY WITH ME. YOUR FURY is turned away, and you have comforted me. I praise you, Lord,
because you were angry with me in persecution, and then afterward your wrath was turned to mercy for me,
and you comforted me in those things. In adversity and in prosperity I praise you, says the holy Church. Behold, God is my Savior.
I will act with confidence and will not fear. See now, God is my Savior. Therefore I act boldly and do not care what man may do to me.
For the Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation. For God is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation.
Therefore I stand boldly in the battle line against my enemies. You shall draw waters with joy from the fountains of the Savior. When the time comes,
then [?] you will draw water with joy out of the fountains of the Savior. In this way you will learn the teaching of the Gospel from him.
His fountains are the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit, from which he gives various gifts to his own. And you shall say on that day: Give thanks to the Lord,
and call upon his name. And then, at the end of the ages, you will say, each one to another: Give thanks to God,
and call upon his name, for his grace is all that we are able to do, the fact that we live, the fact that we exist.
Make known his devices among the peoples. Make known among people his laws, which he has devised for us. Remember
that his name is exalted. Remember that his name is high and glorious in all his works. Sing to the Lord, for he has done magnificently.
Sing to the Lord, for he acted mightily when he appeared in the flesh for the comfort of the whole world. Proclaim this in all the world.
Make it known as far as the world extends. Rejoice and praise, you who dwell in Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel. You, his seat, the watchtower,
you, holy Church, rejoice and praise, because the mighty Holy One of Israel is with you, and you see him, a man among men.
THE CANTICLE OF KING HEZEKIAH. I SAID: IN THE MIDDLE of my days I shall go to the gates of hell.
Hezekiah tells what he thought and what he worried about when he expected to die. I said, in the incompleteness of my days:
Now I am going to hell, for the wicked go there, those who die in the middle of their days because they do not fulfill the works of virtue. Therefore I was afraid for myself.
But the righteous die in the fullness of days, as Abraham died full of days. I sought the remainder of my years.
I sought what was still left to me, sought the fulfillment of my days, so that I might die as Abraham did.
I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living. Alas, I said, I shall not see God; I shall not see him in the land of the living.
I shall no longer look upon man and the inhabitant of rest. From now on I shall not see a worthy man, nor one who is blessed in rest.
I shall not come to the place where God and the good are. My generation is taken away from me and rolled up like a shepherds' tent. Taken
from me is my lineage, from which Christ was to come, and it is torn away just like a shepherd's tent, which does not stand long in one place,
because such tents are moved ever further and further in search of pasture. If you prefer, read: "my generation has rested."
...so it says: "My generation has ceased. My life has been cut off as if by a weaver." My life is cut off,
just as a web is cut by weavers. "While I was still beginning, he cut me off." While I was still thriving in life, God cut me down.
"From morning until evening you will make an end of me." I said to this: From morning until night I wait for recovery, but you make an end of me.
"I hoped until morning; like a lion, so he has broken all my bones." Then again, until morning, I waited for it; I waited for recovery.
How did that go? Like a lion, sickness crushed all my bones. "From morning until evening you will make an end of me. Like the chick of a swallow, so I will cry out;
I will moan like a dove." That is what you do, I said. From morning until evening you make an end of me,
you drive me to death. But I cry out for recovery like a young swallow, and I sigh for it like a dove.
"My eyes are weakened from looking up on high." My eyes have wasted away from gazing up to God
for his help. "Lord, I suffer violence." I also said: I suffer distress, Lord, even beyond my guilt.
"Answer for me." Even if I am guilty, answer for that guilt on my behalf, because it rests with you,
not with me. "For it is not of him who runs or of him who wills, but of God who shows mercy." I did not speak well then, when I was sick;
I should think better of it now that I have recovered. "What shall I say?" What can I say against my Creator? "Or what will he answer me, since he himself has done it?"
Or what does he answer to this if I complain, when he has done just as he wished?
Should one not patiently bear what he determines to do? "I will recount to you all my years in the bitterness of my soul."
In bitterness I recount to you all my years. The years of my reign, which I then thought happy, I now count before you as worthless,
as some comfort for my bitterness, although Epicurus said: "The remembrance of past good things eases present evils."
"Lord, if this is how one lives, and if the life of my spirit is in such things, you will correct me and give me life. Behold, in peace my bitterness is most bitter."
Lord, if human life is like this (I mean in the uncertainty between life and death), and if my life is like this,
caught between the two, what can I say then? Only that you chastise me with sickness and bring me back to life with recovery,
and that is always right. But see, God, that in peace my bitterness was the greatest,
because then I began to draw near to death, when they all began to dwell in peace. When was that?
When the angel of the Lord struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand of Sennacherib's army. Then things began to go well for others and badly for me.
"But you have rescued my soul so that it would not perish; you have cast all my sins behind your back." But you set my soul free
so that it would not be lost; you cast all my sins behind you; you wished your grace to be before my eyes,
not my sins. "For hell will not praise you, nor will death praise you; those who go down into the pit will not wait for your truth."
For hell and death do not praise you, nor do those who go down into the pits of hell. Those [?]
to see the truth of your judgment, but rather your grace. As the grace of Christ has now come about,
in that he went there and set the guilty free. The living, the living shall confess to you, as I also do today.
Rather, it goes like this: the living one praises you, as I live today and praise you. The father shall make your truth known to the sons.
The father makes your truth known to his sons. For so it is written: "Ask your fathers, and they will declare it to you;
your elders, and they will tell you." Lord, save me, and we shall sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.
Preserve me, Lord, and all of us who believe in you, and so we shall sing to you in your temple all the days of our life.
THE CANTICLE OF HANNAH. My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my horn is exalted in my God. My heart rejoiced in the Lord,
says holy Church, for he has opened my womb, which was long barren, and my power is raised up high in him.
That I am queen and rule far and wide comes from him. My mouth is opened wide over my enemies.
My mouth is opened wide over my enemies, for the word of God is not bound, even in the straits of oppression,
even when the preachers themselves are bound, just as Paul did not keep silent when he was in chains. For I have rejoiced in your salvation.
For I have rejoiced in Christ, your Savior. Why should I not? There is none holy as the Lord is, and there is none strong as our God,
for there is no other besides you. There is none so holy and so strong as the Lord our God, nor is there any other besides you who is holier and stronger,
for you can also make others holy and strong. Do not multiply lofty speech, boasting. You boastful Jews,
do not let your proud talk be so much, as though the law could justify you without grace.
Let old things depart from your mouth, for God is the Lord of knowledge. Let old talk be far from your mouth;
avoid empty speech, that is: do not glory in the law. For God is the Lord of all knowledge.
He is the judge of your thoughts. And thoughts shall be prepared for him. And they are laid bare to him.
He knows them better than you do yourselves. Be humble, for whoever thinks himself to be something when he is nothing deceives himself. The bow of the mighty is overcome,
and the weak are girded with strength. The bow of the strong is weakened, the bow of those who presumed that their strength came from themselves,
and the weak have become strong, those who say from the heart: "Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak."
Those who were filled with bread before have been diminished. The Israelites, who were once filled with the divine words, were diminished in their understanding,
because they understood earthly things in the law. And the hungry passed over the earth: and the hungry Gentiles passed over the earth,
because, having come to the faith, they tasted heavenly things in the words of God, not earthly ones. If we read: "Those who were full before hired themselves out for bread,"
And the hungry were filled. That is to say: the Jews, who had formerly been full, became so short of bread that they hired themselves out for it,

because they turned to a foreign understanding, a carnal one and not a spiritual one. But the hungry Gentiles were filled with right understanding. For the barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many
has grown weak. For the Gentile world bore seven, and by these the perfection of the Church is understood. But the Synagogue, which had many children, became sick,
because the weakness of the letter is with her, not the power of the spirit. The Lord kills and makes alive. The Lord kills the one who had children
and brings to life the childless one. He leads down to hell and brings back again. He leads to hell and out of hell. He leads Christ there
and out again. The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and he exalts. The Lord, the Father, makes his Son poor
and makes us rich. He lowers him and raises us up. Raising up the needy from the dust, and lifting the poor from the dung.
Bringing the needy one back to life from the earth, so quickly that he did not see corruption, as in this verse:
"You will not let your Holy One see corruption." And lifting up the poor one from the dung, that is, from the Jews who killed him,
who are rightly called dung, because they lived in earthly thoughts and pleasures of the flesh. So Paul also calls their works dung,
where he says: "What things were gain to me, these I have said to be loss for Christ. And not only losses,
but I have even counted them as dung." That he may sit with princes and hold the throne of glory. That he may sit with the highest ones,
to whom he said: "You shall sit upon twelve seats," and that he may possess the heavenly throne. For the hinges of the earth are the Lord's, and he has set the world upon them.
The hinges of the earth are the Lord's; he set this world upon them. The four regions of the world are his,
and on them he set the world of holy Church, so that his praise may be over all. He will guard the feet of his saints. He guards the feet of his saints
so that they do not walk the wrong way. And the wicked shall fall silent in darkness.
And the Jews will be silenced in their ignorance when the Gospel begins to ring out. For a man is not strengthened by his own strength.
For the faithful people is not strengthened by its own strength but by God's strength. His adversaries will fear the Lord,
and he will thunder over them in the heavens. His adversaries will fear the Lord at the judgment, and then he will thunder over them: "Depart, you cursed, into the eternal fire."
The Lord will judge the ends of the earth. The earth means human beings: when their end comes, the Lord, the Father, will judge them. And he will give dominion to his king
and will exalt the horn of his anointed. And he will give imperial rule to his king, Christ, and will exalt his power.
The Canticle of Moses. Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously magnified; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea. Let us sing to the Lord,
says Moses, for he has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider he threw into the sea. He conquered the devil with his pomps in baptism.
The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation. The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation.
His strength does not let them fall. Therefore those who hold to him do not fall. This is my God, and I will glorify him;
the God of my father, and I will exalt him. This is my God, always the one and the same in the Old and the New Testament.
Not as the heretics would have it, some of whom said one was the author of the Old, and others another of the New. The Lord is like a man of war; Almighty is his name.
The chariots of Pharaoh and his army he has cast into the sea. The Lord is like a warrior; almighty is his name, as is shown in this,
that he cast Pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea. So too he drowns the devil in the abyss of hell. His chosen princes are drowned in the Red Sea.
His chosen princes were drowned in the Red Sea. The chief vices are overthrown by the Lord in the least.
The depths covered them; they went down into the deep like a stone. Deep waters covered them; they went to the bottom like a stone.
The hardness of sin drowned them in hell, because they were not living stones. Your right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength;
your right hand, O Lord, has struck the enemy, and in the multitude of your glory you have put down my adversaries. Your right hand, Lord, is made glorious in its strength;
your right hand struck the enemy, and in the abundance of your glory you put down my enemies. Christ is your right hand;
with him you put down the enemy of our freedom. You sent forth your wrath, which devoured them like stubble [?]. You let loose your anger;
it devoured them as easily as fire devours the stalk. And in the breath of your fury the waters were gathered together.
And in the breath of your anger the waters, which before had stood apart, ran together. The flowing wave stood still;
the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea. Before the good they stood apart; when the wicked came in between them,
then they closed over. The enemy said: I will pursue and overtake; I will divide the spoils; my soul shall be filled;
I will draw my sword; my hand shall slay them. Thus said Pharaoh: I will go after them and seize them; with drawn
sword I will slay them; then I will divide the spoil and have my fill of it. Your breath blew, and the sea covered them;
they sank like lead in the mighty waters. But your breath blew, and then the sea covered them; they sank like lead
in great waters. Who is like you among the mighty, O Lord? Who is like you? Who is like you among strong lords?
Who is like you? Glorious in holiness, terrible and worthy of praise, and doing wonders. Great in deeds in holiness,
terrible in judging, worthy of praise in forgiving, doing wonders. You stretched out your hand, and the earth devoured them. You stretched out your hand,
showed your power, and then the sand covered them. In your mercy you then led your people to the land of promise.
But now you lead the redeemed to the heavenly Jerusalem. And you carried him in your strength to your holy dwelling.
And without his own toil you brought him there, where he would first see the tabernacle, and after that the temple,
just as you now lead the saints into paradise and into heaven. The peoples went up and were angry. Then peoples came against them, settled along the roads.
and they were angered at their journey. Sorrows took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia. The Philistines grieved over it. Then the princes of Edom were troubled.
Then the chief men of the Idumaeans became grieved. Trembling seized the mighty of Moab. Trembling came upon the strongest of the Moabites.
All the inhabitants of Canaan grew rigid. For fear all the settlers of Canaan were struck stiff. Let dread and fear fall upon them in the greatness of your arm.
So may it happen. May fear and pounding of heart fall upon those who begrudged the righteous the journey to heaven. That
in the greatness of your power. Let them become immovable as a stone, until your people pass by, O Lord, until this your people pass through, whom you have possessed.
May they become immovable like the stone, until this your people go and pass through, whom you have possessed.
Until the faithful come fully to rest, whom the devil and his members hasten to lead astray. You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance,
in your most firm dwelling, which you have made, O Lord. You lead them in there, against the will of their enemies, and plant them up there on Mount Zion,
which is your inheritance, that is, the heavenly Jerusalem. There you plant them in your most firm dwelling.
Which is that? The sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands have established. That is the temple, Lord, of the flesh that was taken on,
which human hands did not make, but God's. In it you plant them. The Lord shall reign forever and beyond.
God reigns in eternity and further still. That is said by way of excess, that is, hyperbolically. Much is said beyond
what its sense is. Like this: God, who knows everything, and knows one thing more besides. For Pharaoh went into the sea with his chariots and his horsemen,
and the Lord brought the waters of the sea back over them. Pharaoh with all his men went into the sea, and there the Lord led the sea-waters back over them.
But the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of it. But the sons of Israel went through and out on dry land.
Wherever there is an Egyptian who follows Pharaoh, that is, the devil, he is drowned in the waves of vices. But whoever follows Christ,
to him the waters are a wall on the right and on the left. He goes on dry ground in the middle of the way until he comes out and sings the hymn of victory.
THE CANTICLE OF HABAKKUK FOR SINS OF IGNORANCE. LORD, I HAVE HEARD YOUR REPORT AND WAS AFRAID. The prophet speaks to Christ.
I heard in the spirit what you have resolved to suffer for the human race, and I was terrified at it. Lord, your work in the midst of the years, bring it to life.
Bring that same precious work of yours to fulfillment when its time comes. In the midst of the years you will make it known.
You will show your truth when the fullness of time comes. When you are angry, you will remember mercy. When you are angry with sinners,
then you show mercy again to the repentant. God will come from the south, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. God comes from the south,
he comes from the side of Mount Sinai, which lies by the wilderness that is called Paran. The parents of Christ bring him to Jerusalem from Bethlehem,
which lies to the south, as Paran does too. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise. His glory covered the heavens.
and the earth is full of his praise. As it says: GLORY TO GOD IN THE HIGHEST AND ON EARTH PEACE TO MEN. His brightness shall be like the light.
horns in his hand. His brightness is like light; that means: his fame will give light to those who believe. Horns in his hand:
these are the signs and trophies of the cross. There his strength is hidden. There on the cross he hid his strength, because he did not show it to those
who said: LET HIM COME DOWN NOW FROM THE CROSS AND WE WILL BELIEVE HIM. Death shall go before his face, and the devil shall go out before his feet.
In the desert the tempter met him after he was baptized; there he comes before his feet. He stood and measured the earth.
He looked and broke up the nations, and the mountains of the world were crushed. But Christ stood and surveyed the whole earth.
He looked upon the nations and broke them up, because he dissolved their unbelief, and the proud were humbled to penance.
The hills of the world were bowed down by the journeys of his eternity. The lofty ones bowed down before the journeys of his eternity,
who before his coming were unbending. Because of iniquity I saw the tents of Ethiopia; the skins, that is, the tabernacles of the land of Midian, shall be troubled.
Because of wrongdoing I saw tents become those of demons that should have been temples of God. Because of wrongdoing the tabernacles of Midian, that is, the sinners, will be troubled at the judgment.
Were you angry with the rivers, Lord? Or was your fury against the rivers, or your indignation against the sea? Is your wrath to be against the rivers that flow downward, and against the sea
into which they flow? Not at the first coming, but at the second coming will that happen. Then the worldly will be condemned,
whose minds strive toward lower things. You who will mount upon your horses, and your chariots are salvation. You ride your horses,
because your evangelists, whom you guide, carry you throughout the world, and your chariots are salvation to those who believe in you.
Rousing, you will rouse your bow. You kindle your judgment, by which you show your wrath to the wicked.
The oaths that you spoke to the tribes. You fulfill what you promised to the twelve tribes, that is, to all the faithful,
because you give them eternal life. You will divide the rivers of the earth. You distribute preachers across the earth;
you send them throughout the land. The waters saw you, and the mountains grieved. Through this the peoples came to know you
who did not know you before, and the mighty lamented, so that by mourning they became blessed. The flood of waters passed by. The persecution of the na-
tions passed away, and there was peace. The deep uttered its voice; the height lifted up its hands.
The depth of hearts sounded forth confession; that same depth lifted up its hands in praise. The sun and moon stood still in their dwelling,
in the light of your arrows. Christ and his Church then stood in their place, when Christ sat at the right hand of the Father
and sent her the Holy Spirit, in the openness of your words, which were then understood for the first time. They shall go in the brightness of your flashing spear.
So your spears go shining and flashing. These, again, are the darts of the words of God, heard in darkness and brought forth into light.
In your roaring you will trample the earth; in your fury you will astound the nations. You tread down earthly people in your fury.
you terrify all the peoples in your wrath. When? When you avenge the wrong done to your people. You went forth for the salvation of your people, for salvation with your Anointed.
You, Father, went forth in Christ for the salvation of your people. Together with your Anointed you came to them for salvation.
As it says: "For God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself." What did you do when you came? You struck the head from the house of the wicked.
You slew Antichrist. You took the head away from the house of the evil one, that is, from the world, which is evil. As it says:
"The whole world lies in wickedness." You laid bare the foundation up to the neck. By striking him you laid bare his foundation
up to the neck. All the evils that were his strength you exposed, down to the very worst, on which the head stood.
You cursed his sceptres. You cursed his kingdoms. The head of his warriors, who came like a whirlwind to scatter me. You cursed the struck-off head
of his warriors. You cursed the warriors who came like a whirlwind to scatter me, your people.
Their exultation is like that of one who devours the poor man in secret. Their joy is like the joy of one who rejoices that he may secretly swallow up the poor man.
The evil one swallows him up when he makes him like himself. You made a way in the sea for your horses, in the mud of many waters.
For your preachers you made a way among the nations, in the mud of many waters, that is, in the troubled hearts of the gentiles.
I heard, and my belly, that is, my mind, was troubled. I heard your threats, and they troubled my mind.
At the voice my lips trembled. At their voice my lips trembled, so dreadful are they.
Let rottenness enter into my bones, and let it swarm beneath me. Not only trembling, but rot as well, may it come into my bones,
and may it turn to worms in me, as happened to Job. So that I may rest in the day of tribulation, and that I may go up to our people who are girded.
On these terms: that I may rest in the day of tribulation, and that I may go to our people, who are girded for a good journey.
For the fig tree will not blossom, and there will be no fruit on the vines. For the fig tree does not blossom, and there will be no wine in the vineyards.
When Christ comes, the synagogue, which was the Lord's fig tree and vine, bears no sweet fruit. The work of the olive will fail,
and the fields will yield no food. Then the work of the olive tree will deceive him, and the lands will bear no crops.
What they promised when they said, "All that the Lord has commanded we will do," they prove false. The sweetness of faith or of good
works they do not show. The flock will be cut off from the fold, and there will be no herd in the stalls. The small livestock will be taken from the fold;
no cattle stand at the manger. They have the mangers of the heavenly scriptures, but they do not have the heavenly understanding of them. But I will rejoice in the Lord
and I will exult in God, my Jesus. But I rejoice in the Lord's protection, not in my own righteousness, and I rejoice in my Saviour, not in myself.
The Lord God is my strength, and he will make my feet like the feet of harts. God is my strength; he gives me the swiftness of harts to leap over the perils of sins.
And he will lead me upon my high places. And over my heights he leads me. He makes me pass beyond worldly loftiness through the contemplation of heavenly things.
To the victor, singing in psalms. Singing to him, the victor; giving thanks to him. HEAR, O HEAVENS, WHAT I SAY
THE CANTICLE OF DEUTERONOMY. Hear, O heavens, the things I say to the Jews. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let the earth hear the word of my mouth, for what I am to tell them can reach even you, the greatest elements. Let my teaching gather into rain;
let my speech flow like dew. Let my teaching become rain; let my speech flow like dew.
Rain and dew make the earth fruitful; my words make the Jews better. Like a shower upon the grass and like drops upon the herbs.
May they do good in their minds as raindrops do on grass. For I will call upon the name of the Lord. For I speak God's word.
Give greatness to our God. Glorify God as boldly as you can. The works of God are perfect. For his works are perfect,
and all his ways are judgments. And all his ways are judgments: the reason of discernment shines in them. God is faithful,
and without any iniquity, just and right. God is faithful, and without unevenness, just and upright.
They have sinned against him, not his children, in filth. His changelings defiled themselves in idolatry. A depraved and perverse generation.
A wayward and wicked race. Is this what you render to the Lord, O foolish and unwise people? Do you repay God like this, foolish and witless people?
Is he not your father who possessed you, and made you and created you? Is he not your father, who made you and created you
and possessed you as his inheritance? Remember the days of old, consider each generation. Remember the old days; think on each generation: Abraham,
Isaac, Jacob, how he then, in their times, chose you in them. Ask your father, and he will declare it to you;
your elders, and they will tell you, when the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam. Ask your father and your forebears; they will tell you
when God divided the nations, when long ago, before the Flood, he separated the sons of Adam and would not let the sons of God, descended from Seth, mingle with the sons of men
who came from Cain. From this you can know what danger it is for you, descended from Abraham, to mingle yourself with the gentiles.
He set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel. He set the bounds of the blessed people according to the multitude of the angels,
so that as many of the elect would come from earth to heaven as there remained of the angels when the demons fell. Why do you not hasten there, since you
are invited there? The gentiles, who are idolaters, do not come there. But the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the cord of his inheritance.
But his people is his portion; Jacob is the rope of his inheritance. He is his portion according to election. He found him in a desert land,
in a place of horror and of vast wilderness. He found him in a waste land, in a dreadful wilderness, immeasurably wide,
which is in Arabia, around Mount Sinai. He led him about and taught him. He guided him around the long way of the desert
and trained him there. And he kept him as the apple of his eye. And he guarded him as his own eye.
As an eagle calling its young to fly and hovering over them. Just as the eagle coaxes its young out of the nest
when it wants to make them fly, and flutters above them, so he taught him to come from vices to virtue.
He spread out his wings, and took him, and carried him on his shoulders. He spread out his wings and took him up onto himself,
and carried him on his shoulders, as the eagle does with its exhausted young. Wherever he was in need,
there he helped him. The Lord alone was his leader, and there was no foreign god with him. He alone was his leader,
and no foreign god was with him; he made him believe that there is no other God. He set him upon a high land
so that he might eat the fruits of the fields. He set him on a high land so that he might enjoy the produce of the earth. It is called high because
one travels from Egypt up into the mountains to get there. That he might suck honey from the rock and oil from the hardest stone. That he might suck honey out of the stone,
and oil out of the hardest stone. That means: to have an abundance of all good things. But in the mystical sense: that from Christ, who
is [?], he should learn the Gospel before the Passion, and after the Passion he should receive the Holy Spirit. Butter from the herd:
teaching from the apostles and prophets. And milk from the sheep: admonition from the simple. With the fat of lambs and of rams, the sons of Bashan:
together with the examples of masters and of those under them. And goats with the marrow of wheat, and that they might drink the purest blood of the grape, that is, the most pure.
By this he signified the penitent, when he would eat and drink the body and blood of the Lord. The beloved grew fat and kicked.
With all those good things he was fattened, and then he kicked. Fattened, grown fat, swollen. He did that once he was fattened,
grown fat, swollen. He forsook God his maker and departed from God his saviour. His creator, who was meant to keep him,
he forsook; he turned away from him. They provoked him with foreign gods, and with abominations they stirred him to anger.
With foreign gods they angered him, and with loathsome things they enraged him. They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know.
They sacrificed to devils, not to God; to those who were not known to them, for they would have been hateful to them
if they had known them. New and recent ones came, whom their fathers did not worship. One after another they came,
gods whom their forefathers did not worship. You have forsaken the God who begot you, that is, formed you, and you have forgotten the Lord your creator.
You forsook the one who created and formed you; you forgot him. The Lord saw and was stirred to anger,
because his sons and daughters provoked him. God saw this; therefore he grew angry,
because those whom he had chosen to be his sons and daughters angered him. And he said: And then he said: I will hide my face from them;

Fire is kindled in my wrath; it burns down to the bottom of hell. My vengeance begins to fall on the impious here,

But because of the wrath of the enemies I put it off, lest perhaps their enemies should grow proud. But I postponed it because of their enemies' anger,

Our great power did it all, not God. So he still postpones the punishment of sinners and waits for repentance,

Let them rise up and help you, and protect you in your need. Now is the time; now let them rise up and help you and shield you in distress.
See that I alone am, and there is no other god besides me. Recognize by this that I alone am God, and there is no other but me.

just as in battle, too, the sign that is on shields or in agreed watchwords is called a 'symbolum'; by it each man recognizes his comrades.

For he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid. For he looked upon, that is, deigned to regard, the lowliness of his handmaid.

the old deed of proud Eve. For behold, from this time all generations shall call me blessed. Behold, from now on they will call me blessed,

The faith of Saint Athanasius the bishop. Whoever wishes to be saved, before all things it is necessary that he hold the catho-
-lic faith. Whoever wishes to be saved, for him it is needful before all things that he have the common faith.
Unless a person keeps this faith whole and inviolate, without doubt he will perish forever. Whoever does not keep it whole and uncorrupted
will be lost forever. And the catholic faith is this: that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity,
neither confounding the persons nor dividing the substance. That is the universal faith: that we honor one God in Trinity
and Trinity in Unity, neither mixing the persons nor dividing the substance. The undivided substance shows us one God; the three distinct persons
show us three correlative names of the Trinity. What are correlative names (gagennemmeda), except what in Latin are called relationes? One relation is that of the Father to the Son,
the second is that of the Son to the Father, the third is that of the Holy Spirit to the Father and the Son. Each of these has its own person, as it says further on:
For one is the person of the Father, another of the Son, another of the Holy Spirit. One person is the Father's, another the Son's, the third the Holy Spirit's.
Persons are not understood in God in the same way as in creatures. In creatures there are three persons and three substances, but in God there are three persons and one substance.
Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, or likewise Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, are three persons and three substances; but the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are not three substances,
but three manifestations of the relations that are understood in God. But it is difficult to explain the word persona, because the name was taken from far afield.
When the ancients long ago sat in the theater for plays, their delight at times was to hear mournful songs, which are called tragedies.
In these the weeping of the wretched was imitated, according to the difference of sex and age, so that with feigned voices one made a representation of Priam,
or Hector, or Hecuba, or Andromache, or of anyone whose misfortune the play told of.
Because the actors did this imitation by twisting their mouths, that is, by grimacing, and this seemed unseemly to their spectators,
they therefore began to cover their faces with hollowed pieces of wood, which the Latins now call larvae. Out of these shells, straight through the hollow,
the voice rang out more loudly, and for that reason they were called personae, from personando ("sounding through"). That is where the name personae began, which the Greeks call prosopa,
from covering the face. After that, individual human beings were called personae, and so was every rational creature.
which are distinguished from others by their own property; just as on the stage, sex and age were distinguished by the variety of the voices.
For this reason there are also said to be three persons in grammar: I, you, he; because by them all representations and distinctions of rational beings are made.
It is also toward this that what we read in the Gospel points: "For you do not regard the person of men," which we can interpret as:
"You do not pay heed to human standing." In this way, because of the likeness, the term "persons" came to be carried over [?] to the distinction within the Holy Trinity.
But we must consider what it signifies, not where it was derived from, and, if it is allowed, say "three persons,"
that is, three representations, three manifestations. Of what? Of the relations, as was said before. "But of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit there is one divinity, equal
glory, coeternal majesty." But there is one Godhead of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
equal glory, coeternal might. "Such as the Father is, such is the Son, such is the Holy Spirit."
Such as the Father is in his might, in his power, in his Godhead, such is the Son, such is the Holy Spirit.
"The Father uncreated, the Son uncreated, the Holy Spirit uncreated." The Father is uncreated, the Son is uncreated, the Holy Spirit is uncreated.
"The Father immeasurable, the Son immeasurable, and the Holy Spirit immeasurable." The Father is immeasurable, the Son immeasurable, the Holy Spirit immeasurable.
No mind can measure and comprehend him, because he is present and whole in all places. "The Father eternal,
the Son eternal, and the Holy Spirit eternal." The Father eternal, the Son eternal, the Holy Spirit eternal;
that is, without beginning and without end. "And yet not three eternals, but one eternal." And yet not three eternal ones,
but one eternal one. "Just as there are not three uncreated nor three immeasurable, but one uncreated and one immeasurable." So too there are not three uncreated ones
nor three immeasurable ones, but one uncreated one and one immeasurable one. "Likewise the Father almighty, the Son almighty,
the Holy Spirit almighty." In the same way the Father is almighty, the Son almighty, the Holy Spirit almighty. If he could do evil,
or die, or be brought to an end, or be deceived, that would amount to weakness. "And yet not three almighty ones,
but one almighty." And yet not three almighty ones, but one almighty one. "So the Father is God, the Son is God,
and the Holy Spirit is God." So the Father is God, the Son is God, the Holy Spirit is God. "And yet not three Gods, but there is one God." And yet
they [?] three Gods, but one God. "So the Father is Lord, the Son is Lord, and the Holy Spirit is Lord." So the Father is Lord,
the Son is Lord, the Holy Spirit is Lord. "And yet not three Lords, but there is one Lord." And yet they are not three Lords,
but one Lord. "For just as we are compelled by Christian truth to confess each person individually to be God and Lord,
so we are forbidden by the catholic religion to speak of three Gods or Lords." For just as we must confess each person, taken individually, to be God and Lord,
so we may not say three Gods or three Lords, according to truth and according to right faith.
The Father is made by none, neither created nor begotten. The Father is not made, nor created, nor born.
The Son is of the Father alone, not made nor created, but begotten. The Son is of the one, the Father, not made, nor created,
but born. The Holy Spirit is of the Father and the Son, not made, nor created, nor begotten, but proceeding. The Holy Spirit is of the Father
and of the Son, not made, nor created, nor born, but come forth. So there is one Father, not three Fathers;

And in this Trinity there is nothing that is earlier, nothing that is later, nothing that is greater,

-ity is to be worshipped. So that in every way, as was also said before, threeness is to be honoured in oneness

But it is also needful for eternal blessedness that he also believe faithfully in the humanity of our Lord,

That is the right faith: that we believe and confess that our Lord, the anointed Saviour, the Son of God,
is God and man. He is God, begotten of the substance of the Father before the ages, and he is man, born in the world of the substance of his mother. He is God, born before the world
of the Father's substance, and he is man, born here in the world of the mother's substance. Perfect God, perfect man,

therefore he is true man. Equal to the Father according to the Godhead, less than the Father according to the humanity. The Father's equal in Godhead,

-ity into God. He is one, not in that the Godhead changed itself into manhood,

neither of them became the other. One altogether, not by confusion of substance, but by unity of person. He is one, not from a mixing of the substances,
